title: Dirty Red, Shorty and David, and Grace Carter
summary: Phillips tells about the performers: the blues singer Dirty Red fired in Tampa, the David and Goliath act, and singer Grace Carter who fell ill in Atlanta.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, you mentioned Dirty Red from the carnival show. Tell us a little bit about him. He was a blues singer, right?

A blues singer, yeah, and a dancer -- and a comedian; he told jokes and things. But he could sing the blues real good. He got fired. Mr. Young fired him in Tampa, Florida. That's where we left him, in Tampa.
From the carnival show.
Yes.
He didn't go into vaudeville.

No, he didn't go. Because he couldn't go on account of something was wrong with his bladder. He had to have a place to stay by himself. Because you know, he wetted in the bed... So we left him in Tampa, Florida. That's the last time I saw him.
Then we had another act on the show called Shorty and David. David and Goliath -- Shorty. Goliath was Shorty -- Goliath, just like in the Bible.
And they, too, were in the carnival show.
Yeah, on the carnival and the vaudeville.
David and Goliath were in the vaudeville show.
Yes. Then they had another girl on there singing, she was kind of new, and her name was Grace Carter. But she got sick on the show in Atlanta, and she had to go
Phillips - 38
home, while we were playing the Eighty-One Theatre.
So she was in the carnival show, and then she went to the first date, the first vaudeville date, but didn't make it after that.
Well, yeah.
Grace Carter was a singer.
She was singing and dancing in the chorus, too.
She was one of those six girls?
Yes, she was one of them.
Did she get replaced by anybody?
